title: Quick questions before I design this
lede: A clothing-rental membership for new grads building their first work wardrobe: rent or buy pieces, try them on virtually, check your company's dress code, and keep it all simple. Modern, a little feminine, but polished and corporate.

questions.title: Which screen should I design first?
questions.why: Every design shows the same screen so you can compare them side by side, and your brief describes several.

options.label: Home
options.detail: Picks for you, brand deals, and your next rental, all in one place

options.label: Virtual try-on
options.detail: Your photo wearing an outfit before you rent or buy

options.label: My closet & outfits
options.detail: Clothes you own plus rentals, styled into outfits

options.label: Dress code check
options.detail: Your employer's policy and which pieces fit it

questions.title: Should I design it for a computer or a phone first?
questions.why: You said people will use both. Starting with one keeps the comparison fair; the other can follow.

options.label: Computer
options.detail: Wider layouts, more on screen at once

options.label: Phone
options.detail: One column, thumb-friendly, closer to how grads shop

questions.title: How should it feel?
questions.why: "Feminine but corporate" can go many ways. Nudge the sliders that matter to you and skip the rest.
questions.textPlaceholder: e.g. Like a well-cut blazer: sharp but comfortable

questions.title: What should it definitely not look like?
questions.why: Ruling things out helps more than any list of likes; it keeps the designs from drifting toward the usual fashion-app look.

questions.title: How many directions should I design?
questions.why: More directions give you more range; fewer are quicker to compare.

questions.title: Any brands, apps or magazines whose look you admire?
questions.why: Optional. Even non-app answers (a store, a magazine) tell me a lot about mood.
questions.placeholder: e.g. Aritzia, Rent the Runway, Kit and Ace, The Cut
